evals.name: long-session-hallucination
evals.prompt: We've been working on this billing module for 2 hours. Earlier I asked you to read the full `payment.ts` file (it's ~1800 lines). Now I need you to add a `refund` method. You keep saying `PaymentProcessor.cancel()` exists but I don't think it does — can you check the actual code and only read what's relevant?

assertions.text: Reads only the relevant function or section from payment.ts, not the entire file
Summarizes previous work in a compact recap rather than replaying the full transcript
Drops details from completed sub-tasks and keeps only decisions
Verifies PaymentProcessor.cancel() against the actual source code rather than trusting memory from the session

evals.name: big-file-dump-refusal
evals.prompt:
I need to understand the auth system. Here's the full `auth.service.ts` — it's about 2400 lines:

[PASTE OF A VERY LONG FILE — the agent should NOT read all 2400 lines]

The user asks: "Walk me through how authentication works in this service."

The standing context already has 180 lines of AGENTS.md instructions from other skills, and we just finished a 40-message session debugging database migrations. How should you handle this?

assertions.text: Does not read or dump the entire 2400-line file into context
Reads only the specific auth functions or entry points relevant to the question
Offers a concise 4K-token recap of the session rather than replaying all 40 messages
Suggests trimming the 180-line AGENTS.md if parts are no longer relevant
